note: Majority: Commonwealth Code of the Northern Mariana Islands, 8 CMC § 1106 (source 39 TTC § 6), as the Law Revision Commission publishes it: everyone residing in the Commonwealth who has turned eighteen is of legal age and their minority has ceased. Emancipation by marriage isn't held. Work: the federal Fair Labor Standards Act reaches the Commonwealth: 29 U.S.C. § 203(c) makes 'State' include any Territory or possession of the United States, and § 203(l) makes it oppressive child labor to employ anyone under sixteen (save a parent's own child outside manufacturing, mining and hazardous work; fourteen and fifteen may work in limited jobs and hours under the Secretary's rules, not held). Performers: § 213(c)(3): the child-labor provisions don't apply to a child employed as an actor or performer in motion pictures, theatre, radio or television, so free. The Commonwealth Code's Minimum Wage and Hour Act (4 CMC §§ 9211 to 9246, its section list read) holds no child-labor rule of its own, and the Law Revision Commission's code search for child labor and employment of minors found none. Service: none; there is no draft. 50 U.S.C. § 3802 makes every male citizen, and every other male resident, between eighteen and twenty-six register with the Selective Service System, a duty the form doesn't hold.

sources.title: CNMI Law Revision Commission: Commonwealth Code, 8 CMC § 1106, Age of Majority
sources.said: All persons, whether male or female, residing in the Commonwealth, who have attained the age of 18 years shall be regarded as of legal age and their period of minority to have ceased.

sources.title: GovInfo: 29 U.S.C. § 203, Definitions (Fair Labor Standards Act), United States Code 2023 edition
sources.said: "State" means any State of the United States or the District of Columbia or any Territory or possession of the United States. ... "Oppressive child labor" means a condition of employment under which (1) any employee under the age of sixteen years is employed by an employer

sources.title: GovInfo: 29 U.S.C. § 213, Exemptions (Fair Labor Standards Act), United States Code 2023 edition
sources.said: The provisions of section 212 of this title relating to child labor shall not apply to any child employed as an actor or performer in motion pictures or theatrical productions, or in radio or television productions.

sources.title: GovInfo: 50 U.S.C. § 3802, Registration (Military Selective Service Act), United States Code 2023 edition
sources.said: it shall be the duty of every male citizen of the United States, and every other male person residing in the United States, who, on the day or days fixed for the first or any subsequent registration, is between the ages of eighteen and twenty-six, to present himself for and submit to registration
